- **Kinase question and Atf4 reconciliation (2026-10-28, step B3 of mandate ORCH-ROADMAP-IT4-20261028; question-driven re-read of the fly paper, staged receipt `FTR-20261028-42909904-03`, partial; first-hand reading of its two cited interactome papers described in `research/drug_repurposing/isr_kinase_interactome_atf4_reconciliation_it4_20261028.md` section 8; EXPLORATORY; NOT WWOX-DEE EVIDENCE; adds no PRO or CONTRA to the WWOX question and changes no status, ranking line or reopening condition).** (1) The fly Atf4 rise is a significant two-group difference in the amyloid background (Mann-Whitney U 0, P 0.0022, 6 vs 6) and a non-significant one without amyloid (t 0.0894, P 0.9305, 6 vs 6); no interaction test is reported, so neither a statistically demonstrated interaction nor a demonstrated absence of effect without amyloid is on record. (2) The Xbp1 reporter (IRE1 arm; t 1.365, P 0.1954, about 15 brains, amyloid background only, no positive control described) is non-significant at low precision; it neither excludes IRE1 nor says anything about PERK, so the paper's Results wording about the PERK-Atf4 branch is an inference by exclusion with PERK, GCN2 and phospho-eIF2 alpha all unmeasured. (3) The two interactome entries behind the Discussion's kinase candidates are weak: GCN1 is a low-score unvalidated prey in a WWOX tandem-affinity purification (HEK293T; interaction score 0.133, 10 spectra over two replicates, below the authors' own 0.2 candidate line; no empty-vector control described), and WWOX is a three-spectrum hit (none in mock cells) in a PERK proximity-biotinylation list (HEK293-T) in which GCN1 is a stronger hit than WWOX; neither shows binding, activation or direction. **Stage 1 design revised:** kinase attribution by genotype x kinase-loss interaction (EIF2AK3, EIF2AK4, EIF2AK1, EIF2AK2) in isogenic knockout and WWOX-corrected neural cells at matched maturity, with a vehicle, an amyloid-beta oligomer and a non-amyloid challenge and acute and chronic time points; inhibitors only as support (two chemotypes, dose-response, target-engagement readout), because GSK2606414-class compounds have a RIPK1 liability, GCN2 ATP-competitive inhibitors can activate GCN2 at low doses, and an eIF2B activator acts downstream of all four kinases so it cannot assign a kinase (the last two are from memory and unverified here).
